subject: OnPrem patch convoy: schedule, net-drain play and pinning plan
raw_thread:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Rios <samantha@greenleafhealth.com>, ops@greenleafhealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: OnPrem patch convoy: schedule, net-drain play and pinning plan

Hi Samantha / Greenleaf ops team —

Thanks for taking the time on short notice. Per our intake call last week, we want to lock down a confined maintenance window for the on-prem Redwood Private deployment (vpc cluster: glh-prod-1) to apply a small security patch (serving runtime 1.12.4 -> 1.12.5) and a driver micro-update for the network agents. Key asks from our side:

- A 3-hour narrow window where API traffic is allowed to be routed to standby nodes (we plan a rolling convoy, not a full freeze).
- Network-drain access for the ops runbook below (we'll provide commands) and a single point of contact on your side for bridge-level changes.
- Confirmation on KMS rotation policy window: any KMS key rotations must be blocked during patching to avoid transient auth failures.

Attached: patch-convoy-runbook.md (detailed step-by-step), net-drain-commands.sh (drain + uncordon helpers), maintenance-timeline.csv (proposed run-of-show).

High-level plan (proposed):
1) 00:00–00:20 — preflight checks and telemetry snapshot (all regions).
2) 00:20–01:40 — rolling patch convoy across 4 node groups; 1 group at a time; canaries at 10% traffic for 15m after each group.
3) 01:40–02:15 — soak and validation (latency/cost checks).
4) 02:15–03:00 — emergency rollback window and post-mortem capture.

Version pinning note: we recommend pinning customer-critical routes to runtime 1.12.4 during the window until the first successful canary completes, then remove pin incrementally. If you prefer to keep strict pinning until full fleet success, we'll need an explicit unpin approval from your security lead.

Questions for you before we finalize:
- Can you confirm the blackout constraints (any business units that cannot have even short canaries)?
- Who will be our bridge lead (name + cell)?
- Do you need us to avoid any node-level driver restarts (some hardware controllers on-prem require manual handshake)?

I'll follow up with a short doc that enumerates rollback commands and observable thresholds (error rate + avg latency) that trigger abort.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Platform PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

----

From: Samantha Rios <samantha@greenleafhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@greenleafhealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:15:42 -0500
Subject: Re: OnPrem patch convoy: schedule, net-drain play and pinning plan

Hi Alex,

Appreciate the clear runbook. Quick answers below:

- Blackout constraints: the billing and patient ingestion systems (lane A and lane B) cannot be impacted during 06:00–13:00 ET; we can accept a maintenance window starting 00:00–03:00 ET.
- Bridge lead: Marcus Chen (mobile: +1-617-555-0142) — he'll be on the bridge for the whole window.
- Driver restarts: we have one rack (rack-7) with legacy controllers; avoid automated driver reboots there — we'll do manual handoff if needed.

We also require that any KMS rotation or schema migration be blocked for 24 hours before and after the maintenance window; our compliance team wants that logged.

Samantha
Samantha Rios
Head of Infrastructure
Greenleaf Health

----

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Rios <samantha@greenleafhealth.com>, ops@greenleafhealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: OnPrem patch convoy: schedule, net-drain play and pinning plan

Thanks Samantha — good constraints. Notes / follow-ups:

- We'll shift the proposed window to 00:00–03:00 ET (which is 21:00–00:00 PT previous night for our ops).
- For rack-7: we'll mark that group as manual-handshake in the runbook and exclude from automated canaries; we'll include an explicit manual step pointing to Marcus.
- KMS rotation: understood. We'll add a preflight check that queries your KMS status and blocks the rollout if rotation_age < 24h.

Karthik / Monica / Markus — can you review the attached net-drain-commands.sh and confirm the drain/un-drain sequence is safe for their network fabric? Specific ask: when we drain a node we need graceful KV cache flush (kv-checkpoint) followed by HUP to agent, then cordon. If natural order is different for GLH infra, call it out.

I'll update the maintenance-timeline.csv and re-attach shortly.

Alex

----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Samantha Rios <samantha@greenleafhealth.com>, ops@greenleafhealth.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:42:55 -0700
Subject: Re: OnPrem patch convoy: schedule, net-drain play and pinning plan

Alex / Samantha — quick ops check after reviewing net-drain-commands.sh:

1) Sequence is fine but two changes recommended for Greenleaf fabric:
   - Add an explicit 'sync-kv --wait 30s' between kv-checkpoint and HUP for the legacy controllers to ensure cache persistence on rack-7.
   - Use 'net-qos hold' on the management VLAN before uncordon to avoid transient spikes in control-plane traffic.

2) Rollback: implement a three-step rollback guard in runbook (we already put this in patch-convoy-runbook.md):
   - immediate: mark node read-only and shift traffic to standby; restore previous runtime package (1.12.4) from pinned image; restart agent.
   - short-term: if read-only nodes exceed threshold for 15m, execute fleet-wide unpin and staged restore of route pins.
   - long-term: escalate to a formal postmortem and schedule a hotfix slot.

3) Observability thresholds: abort if error rate >3% for 10m OR median latency increases >120% over baseline for 5m. We'll collect these via the ops bridge dashboards and stream to your NOC channel.

I'll attach a short diff to the runbook with the sync-kv line and QoS hint. Marcus — tagging you: please confirm manual handoff for rack-7.

Karthik
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

----

Attachments referenced:
- patch-convoy-runbook.md (see section 4.2: canary gating + rollback ladder)
- net-drain-commands.sh (drain -> sync-kv -> hup -> cordon -> verify)
- maintenance-timeline.csv (updated with ET/PT mapping)

Next steps agreed:
- Alex to push final timeline and attach updated runbook with Karthik's diffs (by EOD PST Thu).
- Greenleaf to confirm Marcus on the bridge and finalize blackout acceptance (Samantha).
- Karthik to add the quick QoS hold and KV sync lines to runbook.
